source: The FA / Essex FA — Mini-Soccer and Youth Futsal Handbook 2025
note: Chris's activities are tagged ks1 / lks2 / uks2 (roughly Y1-2 / Y3-4 / Y5-6). KS1 and most of LKS2 sit inside this handbook's mini-soccer age bands (U7-U10). UKS2 (Y5-6) typically plays 9v9, which is outside mini-soccer and not covered by this handbook.

miniSoccer.intro: Development football for U7-U10 — the emphasis is maximising touches, involvement and enjoyment over result.

ageGroups.duration: Max 40 min per day (can be split into quarters)
Max 60 min per day (can be split into quarters)

keyRules.title: No offside
keyRules.detail: Offside is not played in development mini-soccer — the pitch stays open for everyone to get on the ball.

keyRules.title: No throw-ins
keyRules.detail: Replaced with a pass or dribble back into play from the touchline — keeps the ball moving and skills in play.

keyRules.title: No deliberate heading
keyRules.detail: Punishable by an indirect free kick to the opposition.

keyRules.title: Retreat line
keyRules.detail: The defending team must retreat to the halfway line while the goalkeeper takes a goal kick.

keyRules.title: Rolling substitutions
keyRules.detail: Roll-off, roll-on subs can be made at any time with the referee's permission, and a substituted player may come back on later.

keyRules.title: Equal game time
keyRules.detail: Every player on the squad should get at least 50% of the game.

keyRules.title: Power Play
keyRules.detail: A team losing by 4 or more goals may add an extra player to help even the game back up.

keyRules.title: Goalkeeper restriction
keyRules.detail: A GK can't pick up a ball deliberately kicked to them by a teammate — that gives away a free kick on the edge of the penalty area. GKs wear a shirt in a different colour to outfield players.

trophyEvents.note: Max 3 trophy events across the season, each running over 2 weeks.
Max 3 trophy events across the season, each running over 4 weeks.

youthFutsal.intro: 5-a-side on a hard court — same touches-and-decisions philosophy as mini-soccer, adapted for a smaller, faster indoor game.
youthFutsal.format: 5v5 on court, squads of up to 14
youthFutsal.ball: Size 3 (U12 and under) · Size 4 (U13 and above)
youthFutsal.pitch: Hard court — indoors preferred, outdoor hard surface acceptable. Never grass or artificial grass (3G/AGP). Marked touchlines, no walls or boards.
youthFutsal.goal: 3m × 2m (the same size as a hockey or handball goal); posts and crossbar must contrast with the pitch colour
youthFutsal.duration: Two 20-minute halves, running time — the clock stops whenever the ball goes out of play. One 60-second timeout per team, per half.

keyRules.title: 4-second rule
keyRules.detail: The player restarting play (kick-in, corner, free kick, goal clearance) has 4 seconds to put the ball back into play.

keyRules.title: GK 4-second limit
keyRules.detail: A goalkeeper can't control the ball for more than 4 seconds while it's in their own half.

keyRules.title: No back-passes to the GK
keyRules.detail: A deliberate pass back to the goalkeeper is not allowed to be handled.

keyRules.title: 5-metre rule
keyRules.detail: Opponents must retreat 5m at every restart — kick-ins, goal clearances, free kicks and corners.

keyRules.title: 6-metre penalty ('the D')
keyRules.detail: Penalties are taken from 6m, on the edge of the penalty arc.

keyRules.title: No sliding tackles
keyRules.detail: Not permitted for U16 and under, except to keep the ball in play (not to challenge an opponent).

keyRules.title: Accumulated fouls
keyRules.detail: 5 direct free kicks against a team in a half are free kicks as normal; the 6th foul in that half gives a 10m penalty instead.

keyRules.title: Red card
keyRules.detail: The offending team plays with 4 players until either 2 minutes have passed or the opposition scores — whichever comes first.
